heading: How a Northwind blanket is made
intro: Four stages, one state, nothing rushed.

items.title: Fleece from two farms
items.text: Wool from two Willamette Valley flocks, bought at a fair price each spring.

items.title: Spun in Oregon
items.text: A family mill in Salem spins it into a soft two-ply yarn, undyed or dyed in small lots.

items.title: Woven on a 1960s loom
items.text: Aiko weaves each throw on a restored Dobcross loom. About three hours a blanket.

items.title: Finished by hand
items.text: Washed, brushed and checked twice before it is folded into tissue and boxed for you.
